gateway.text:
**Simple comparison:** a personalized cancer vaccine **teaches the patient’s own immune system what to look for**. Engineered cell therapy **adds a chosen recognition receptor to immune cells before—or sometimes inside—the body**.

- **Personalized cancer vaccine:** Researchers start with tumor-specific DNA changes, then check whether the altered message is expressed, processed into a peptide, displayed by the patient’s HLA molecule, and recognized by T cells. The vaccine helps prime and expand those T cells. It does not guarantee that every tumor cell displays the target, or that the response will kill cancer [vaccine overview](/education/guides/personalized-cancer-vaccine/index/#the-big-ideas) [target selection](/education/guides/personalized-cancer-vaccine/02-reading-tumor-and-normal-data/).

- **Engineered cell therapy:** Researchers install a receptor with a defined target. A **CAR** usually recognizes an accessible molecule directly on the tumor-cell surface. A conventional **TCR** recognizes an internal protein only after it is processed into a peptide and displayed with HLA. Target selection therefore asks both, “Will the receptor recognize enough tumor?” and “Could it also attack healthy tissue?” [cell-therapy overview](/education/guides/engineered-cell-therapy/index/#the-big-ideas) [target selection](/education/guides/engineered-cell-therapy/02-choosing-a-target/#specify-the-target-at-the-level-the-receptor-reads).

**Analogy:** a vaccine distributes a wanted poster and trains local officers; engineered cells are issued officers carrying a specific scanner.

Would you like a simple side-by-side example comparing a **neoantigen vaccine**, a **CAR**, and a **TCR therapy**?
